newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Macedonia to get $70 million in economic aid.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia to get $70 million in economic aid.

text.p: The former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia has been promised $70 million by donor groups to aid its economic reconstruction efforts.

Kenneth Lay, director of the World Bank's southeastern Europe department, told a news conference that the money would go a long way towards helping Macedonia continue its "remarkable and successful progress towards market reform".
He was speaking at the end of a two-day donor conference on Macedonia organised by the bank and the European Commission.
"More than any other country in the region, Macedonia has adopted and aggressively pursued the kind of reform we want to see," Lay said.
"It has't been easy, but Macedonia is an island of stability in a very difficult area."
Jane Miljovski, Macedonia's deputy prime minister, told the same news conference that his country was determined to pursue open market policies.

"Already we can boast of some success," he said. "There was two percent growth last year and we predict five percent in 1997. Inflation is down from 2,000 percent a few years ago to less than two percent this year."
But Miljovski admitted his country still faced many problems -- particularly with unemployment and attracting foreign private investment.

"Our unemployment rate (35 percent) terrifies economists, but we have reason to believe our methodology may be at fault," he said. "Unemployment is high, however, and reducing it remains a top priority."
He said also that regional unrest -- including political disturbances in neighbouring Albania -- continued to discourage investors.
Macedonia wanted now to concentrate on privatising the remaining enterprises still under state control, Miljovski said, adding over 90 percent had already been transformed.
The $70 million pledged by 26 bi- and multi-lateral donors during the Brussels meeting comes mainly in the form of grants and soft loans, Lay said.
